author: Raylyn W

title: Completely worth it. Amazing app for ADHD brains
body: This app is one of the most useful tools I've ever used to combat procrastination and other ADHD related difficulties. I love how flexible it is to be able to adapt to what I specifically need. I especially love that I can skip a part of my routine and it still marks the entire routine as completed (you can see in the details what you skipped). This is a big deal for me because it removes the feeling of missing something and the guilt that could entail. People often say "just start" but it feels like every part of a bigger task needs that decision to start. With this app, I just need to decide to start the routine, the rest is decided. It's gotten me to be more consistent with my workouts (I just added 15 minutes of yoga to the end of my morning routine) and with my studies. But I use it for anything I do regularly that involves more than two sequential actions. The big thing is, YOU need to decide start. The app can remind you, but only you have the power to take that action. But once you've done that, the app (and your past self who created the routine) removes the decision fatigue from the rest of that routine. I seriously and wholeheartedly recommend this app!

body: This app is garbage now. They changed the alarm so that it now only plays sound instead of making your phone vibrate. They also changed the alarm notification to look like an actual alarm, meaning you can just shut it off. The appeal of Routinery for me was that the alarm would push constant notifs to my phone and make it buzz with no way to turn it off except to start the routine. That always forced me to remember what I need to do. Without that, I know I'll just end up dismissing or missing entirely the notifs the app sends. It's useless now. Im canceling my subscription after being a loyal customer for years. Devs, please restore the old functionality and give us an option of vibrate-only alarms and push notifications that don't stop until you begin the routine!
author: skywardly

title: It’s great. Pay them for their hard work if you find it useful.
body: NOTE: being mad an app isn’t free is like being mad restaurants aren’t free or your plumber isn’t free. I guarantee you that hundreds, if not thousands of hours went into making this app, and it’s updated constantly… which means they’re working on it all the time. If you value someone’s work, you should pay them for it. Having a concentration app shoving ads in your face constantly worlds kind of defeat the purpose, no? Regarding the app: I needed a relatively simple app to break my day into blocks of repeatable tasks (e.g. morning routine) and blocks of time where I could use my existing task management tools to get things done. This app is great for that. Not as rigid as Tiimo time-wise but it’s heavier on reminders. Tiimo ended up being a place where I could see whatever it was that I’d been falling to work on for the past hour… this does a better job of keeping me on track. Support (might be a one person project?) is responsive and useful. Syncing for the watch is excellent while in a routine (another thing Tiimo was terrible at)    -Wishes- Base Functionality: * Halfway reminders, or reminders every 𝑛 minutes would be super useful. While I’m working, I use an interval timer app that gives me a simple notification every six minutes. Having this integrated would be helpful. * would love a mode where I had a pile of tasks and a set block of time and I could choose which ones to do next. Sometimes it doesn’t matter if I shave before a brush my teeth but just need to be reminded to do both and stay on task. UI improvements: * Having text search of emoji would help. Doesn’t have to be any more complicated than a filter based on characters included in the name. Figuring out whether the icon I want is in default or whatever can be tedious. “Wait… was there a work category? No? Maybe electronics? No… hmmm” * Having sub-headings or details under title for tasks would be helpful. * Still not really sure what contexts are. My first guess is that they’d be like GTD contexts like “on the phone,” or “at work,” but that doesn’t really make sense for a scheduled task. Maybe that’s not the right word for the functionality? If so, some other wording could use cleanup— “you can restart at any time” implies that you’re starting from the beginning. Unless I’m not seeing the ability to restart, it should read “you can continue any time.” In think there are a few other minor ones but clearly not important enough to matter. * Would love to see a breakdown of how much time I allocated to each task in reality so I can adjust my schedule or habits. That is more important info to me than whether or not I completed the entire block exactly as prescribed. Thanks for making the app.

I do like that you can pause a task because let’s face it, we’re not all going to get dressed in under 5 minutes flat every day. Overall, it’s a nice app and I think I will continue to use it. Other apps like this one I found to not hold the accountability that this one does. It would be too easy to push it off, whereas this one has timers, reminders and really helps my neuro spicy ADHD self to get my morning routine done and taken care of. Give it a try!

title: Work in Progress Habits
body:
I’ve been using Routinery to help restructure my mornings, and as someone who is highly sensitive to overstimulation, I have found it to be a very helpful tool for managing my daily energy.
What I appreciate most is the sequential flow. Instead of feeling overwhelmed by a long list of tasks, the app guides me through one step at a time. It acts as a gentle pacer, which is essential when I’m trying to transition into my workday without feeling drained before I even arrive. It provides a sense of structure that helps me stay grounded when my routine starts to slip.
Overall, it is a great resource for anyone who needs to protect their morning routine and maintain a steady pace throughout the day.
I truly enjoyed using this to build a peaceful morning habit. It is perfect for someone who values slow mornings and wants to focus on healthy habits that provide peace of mind. I was even finding success with my evening routines. Unfortunately, because of the subscription constraints, I am unable to build an afternoon routine, which is a disappointing barrier.
While this is a great tool in theory, I am not pleased with the cost restrictions. I hope to return to the app in the future if there is a way to use it without a financial barrier, but for now, the subscription prevents me from fully integrating it into my life.

My only complaint at the moment: PLEASE PLEASE FIX THE WATCH APP. I know it was recently updated and it’s come a long way but I rely on it and it’s so glitchy. It will regularly just stop mid routine on the watch, completely skip steps, completing the routine on the watch doesn’t register in the app messing with streaks, and the app will say a routine is running on the watch when it isn’t. title: Gone downhill.
body: Recently I’ve had a really terrible experience with this app. It never works right for me. The voice settings randomly switch back and forth from beeps to voice, sometimes it will give me “five minutes until”, sometimes not…the whole point of this app is to make it effortless to help with my routines. I literally spent an entire “routine” trying to adjust my settings on my iPhone, accessibility, widgets, enabled notifications, making sure everything is updated, checking that I wasn’t on “focus” mode…. Nothing worked. The voice alarm settings are wildly inconsistent. Even if there is something I’m missing, I shouldn’t have to go on a whole wild goose chase through my phone. I held off writing this review because I wanted to make sure I was being fair and it wasn’t something I was doing on my end but…literally the voice settings change within the same routine, even if I delete the history and run it again, they will be wildly different the second time around. Awful. If you have ADHD and are looking for a helper app, this is not the one. It has sabotaged me multiple times this week. Which is sad, because it used to work great.

title: Useless app / steals your money
body:
DO NOT DOWNLOAD. DO NOT AGREE TO FREE TRIAL.

I downloaded the app after reading the reviews because I wanted something to help add structure to my mornings. I signed up for the 7-day free trial with the understanding that I’d either cancel before the trial ended or be charged after the 7 days.

Instead, when I opened the app, it asked me to log in if I already had an account. I entered my email and it said I did have one (I must’ve tried this app a long time ago). The second my login went through, it charged me the full YEAR fee immediately.

I did not agree to pay for a full year. I was not warned that logging into an old account would automatically trigger a full annual charge. I never received the free trial I signed up for — I was charged without my approval.

I contacted Apple for a refund literally within minutes of the charge (my bank alerted me almost instantly), and they still refused to refund it even after I explained exactly what happened.

The app is still as useless as it was the first time I tried it — except now I’m forced to pay for a full year of something I don’t want and won’t use, and no one will reimburse me.

This is NOT a case of me forgetting to cancel after the trial. I was charged immediately without consent because I logged into an old account. Misleading and shady.

Save your money. Use Apple Reminders or an app like TickTick instead. DO NOT download.

title: Perfect tool for adulting with Multiple Sclerosis & depression
body:
I was confused about the promotional offer when I got this app and contacted customer service. I got a very thoughtful email from the CEO completely addressing my concerns and asking for any other feedback. I provided one other request for a tweak to an app feature and received another thoughtful response from the CEO. I’m very pleased with the customer service. 

This app helps me like no other app, book, plan, or strategy has been able to do. I struggle with time blindness (losing track of time) and being a time wizard with a broken wand (having no idea how long it actually takes to finish tasks and WAY underestimating). I also have lots of anxiety and motivation but difficulty with task initiation (I want to start, know it’s important, but transitioning from one thing to another or from stopped to moving is REALLY difficult). This app HELPS!

1. My morning routine starts automatically when I turn off my alarm. The first task has a timer on it so I don’t have time to dawdle or hurkle-durkle. I’m pressured to get up and get going. 

2. If I don’t finish a task in the routine within the time limit, it reminds me, aloud, that time is up for that task and I need to move on to the next thing. It will remind me again in another minute, and five minutes after, and ten minutes after. It does not let me off the hook to just wander off task and forget what I’m supposed to be doing. If I’m not doing what I’m supposed to be doing, it is at least a deliberate choice now. 

3. At the end of the routines, it shows how long it ACTUALLY took me to complete each task so I can get a realistic idea of how long muggles take to get ready in the morning (which is important since apparently my wand is broken and I can’t magically shower, get dressed, gather my things, and get in the car all in an instant).

4. Once I’ve entered all the tasks into my routine with a start time, it shows me the finishing time so I know when I’ll really be ready and if I need to get up earlier.

5. Most importantly though is that since every task has a timer on it I feel a sense of pressure to keep moving forward which helps IMMENSELY with task initiation, motivation, staying on task, working quickly, and goal achievement. 

6. I do like that there is a checklist option for items that don’t fit into a routine but that need to be done at some point.

title: Great & Underrated app
body:
I love this app for many reasons. It isn’t magical but it is practical for my neurospicy brain that it feels like it. I love the way it starts with a visual deep breath. 

You set up your own routines as
detailed or as broadly as you need. Or try templates at first. Morning routine, skin care, work  arrival, etc. Whatever routine 

You can have the app vocally narrate the routine, telling you “2 remaining for brush teeth then drink lemon water.” You can skip steps, you can rearrange the order in real time so that on the days where you can’t drink lemon water as your next task you move it to the end so that you still get prompted to do it later. And it doesn’t permanently change the order, just lets today be different. And you can still skip it later in the routine but at least you tried to see if the lemon water might happen after getting dressed. 

This really has helped me habit stack and internalize some groups of actions in ways that head knowledge cannot. But where I may also forever need prompts, this is enjoyable and comforting and motivating. It tells me where I am with timing of tasks so I can both go with the flow but not lose track of my schedule.  It gives tutorials to help automate the start up of the app with my iPhone alarm. 

You do have to do your part and start the ball rolling in some way. If you don’t use it and keep adapting it as you use it then it won’t do you any good. But it has many really useful elements that make it better than setting a million alarms and reminders.

title: Game changer
body:
I don’t write a lot of reviews, but this app has been super helpful in keeping me on top of my daily routines so I feel compelled to write one now! It’s so much easier know to predict how long a routine task might take and to plan my day better, and it feels easier to focus on one task at a time when you know exactly how much time you’ve given yourself until the next task starts.

I do have some critiques, however. Firstly, the robotic text to speech voice is a little bit creepy and assertive. I’d be nice to have more naturalistic voice reminders if possible. Secondly, I’d find it helpful if there was a button to show the average task time since the first completion. The default length of a week is fine, but I’d like there to be an easier way to find the average across all completions than to have to reselect the dates on the calendar for every individual task.

All that being said, highly recommend for anyone looking to give themselves a bit more structure!

title: Very annoying to use
body:
The app is bloated with unnecessary features like social feeds and analytics. I wanted a straightforward habit tracker, not a lifestyle management tool. Its main function—creating habits with timed checklists—sounds good in theory, but in practice it’s rigid. I often multitask or switch the order of habits, which means constant reorganization. The timers create pressure instead of structure, and the voice prompts are intrusive.

The checklist system is the only redeeming feature, but even that lacks basic usability. There’s no quick “reset all” option, and notes for tasks are buried inside menus instead of being visible in the list view. 

The layout is poor. On iPhone it wastes space with oversized design elements, and on larger Android screens it looks cramped and unoptimized. Overall, the experience feels inefficient and overdesigned.

If you just want a clean, flexible daily routine tracker, avoid this one. Todoist and Apple Reminders are better, but Todoist can get cluttered and Reminders doesn’t sync well with Android. This app tries to do everything and ends up doing nothing well.

title: This app keeps me sane (ADHD)
body: I really struggling to keep track of everything I needed to do to get ready in the mornings, and more than once have bcompletely forgot important tasks or objects before leaving for work. I also would often find myself standing in my kitchen trying to remember what else needed to be done, which was both exhausting and stressful. This app ended up being exactly what I needed. I've been using the app for about a year, and what is the most helpful to me is that it's essentially a list that resets itself everyday regardless of what I did or didn't do yesterday, no extra work needed on my part to reset it or fix it. It's also really nice that I can set an approximate amount of time for the task, so I have a better idea of how long I need to get it all done. This app ended up being so successful for what I needed that I started using it before bed as well. Now my laptop is always charged before I leave, the ice packs are frozen in the fridge, and I didn't forget to brush my teeth!

title: Helpful, but lacking
body:
This needs some feature updates for users who aren’t teenagers or young adults. More statistics—mood (not just mood on how do you feel about completing your routine), percentages of routine completed, correlation between mood and percentage of routine completed. 

This could be amazing if they focused less on incorporating things like the community aspect of the app and nonsense like celebrities’ routines and more on actual science and data. If, for example, users could see a positive correlation between completing at least 85% of their routines with an improvement in mood, many would certainly find routines—and this product—to be vital rather than something they downloaded on a whim and won’t renew next year. 

Developers need to consider they’re neglecting an entire pool of serious adult users who are also inclined to have deeper pockets than the teenage and college crowd do.

title: Mental Clarity
body:
I am the mother of a child with severe disabilities.  We have a lot of routine care tasks to track. Routinery has really helped me with mental clarity, and I feel much better since I started using it. i can’t say enough how helpful this app has been for me. 

I do have a wishlist. All of my routines are manual because I don’t start them at the same time each day. I wish there were a way to hide my usual evening tasks (like a bedtime routine) until later in the day because my entire list of daily routines has become too cluttered. I also wish there were seasonal, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual routine options. I also wish there were a way to make certain tasks show up only on certain days. For example, I water my houseplants on each Sunday, but I fertilize them once a month. It would be nice to be able to have it all as part of the same Sunday plant care routine with the fertilizer showing up only once per month.  I know I could duplicate the routine and set them for different Sundays, but any future changes to the routine would require the change to be made to each of those routines. I hope this makes sense.

UPDATE: I love this app, but I have so many routines that I am having difficulty finding and organizing them when I filter by activated routines. I wish there were some way to categorize the routines by day, frequency, and topic (like fitness, household, plants, etc. ) so I could pull them up to make any changes.

title: absolute game changer
body:
This is one of the best apps i’ve ever used. I’ve tried so many routine apps, timers, but this one has been the most helpful so far. the constantly updating reminders of when the next task will start and when it will all end are IMMENSELY HELPFUL for actually keeping me on track/getting back on it after becoming distracted, which is generally my biggest routine struggle. The push notifications that can’t be dismissed are also absolutely crucial. The ability to rearrange tasks and choose to update only today or for all days is also pretty great. I also really enjoy the little in-app encouragements, I didn’t think much about them at first but they add up and are nice to see on bad days. I’ve spent money on premiums for apps before and have mostly been disappointed or frustrated after losing interest- i can honestly say that the paid version of this is absolutely worth it. Unlike most paywalled apps, the free version of this is perfectly good if you only have one or two routines. With no limit, my routines help me get ready for work, decompress at home, take my medication on time, and do my chores.

A feature I think I’d like to see one day would be the ability to add conditions to individual tasks (it only shows up on a Monday, it only shows up after a certain time of day, etc) in a single routine. This way, if my daily routine is the same every day but I have an extra chore to take care of on Mondays and another on Friday, I can have one daily routine that adapts. Currently you can do this by adding the task and simply skipping, but this makes the timers and “all ends” time slightly inaccurate.

Overall, this app has been life changing in taking some weight off my shoulders every day. I hope one day I can develop an app or tool like this that can benefit someone the way this app has benefitted me.

title: Load time and constant reminders already clicked on will make you ADD if you weren’t already
body:
Update 6-4-25: Every update downloaded just makes the app more prone to glitches, freezing and deletion of data. I’ve given the app many months and heard many promises of improvement from the developers. Unfortunately, the function just gets worse. If you have an older iPhone, don’t download this app. It’s poor and inconsistent performance will not ease ADD symptoms but make them worse. 

My original Routinery app review submitted 8-29-24: 
The app gets four stars mostly because of the size of the problem it is trying to solve. However, the biggest reason it gets four stars instead of fewer is that they’re really don’t seem to be any other options for people whose mind works the way mine does. The app is worth the annual fee charged no question. However, a handful of improvements could make it worth two or three times the price and simultaneously still be a five star value! number one decrease the battery usage, especially during longer tasks and with respect to notifications, for example I have an older model iPhone there are two apps on my iPhone that use up one percent of battery almost every minute that I am using that app: Google Maps is one and Routinery is the other. I can sort of understand why Google maps requires so much battery considering the sheer computational power of providing real time traffic information and navigation at such granular detail With street level video. On the other hand, why exactly does Routinery require so much battery? I think it must be a flaw in the design or some non-essential portion of the application that is not being regularly used by the customer are draining the customers device battery. Fix that and I’ll actually be able to use the routines that I created for Routinery currently I cannot— because within an hour and a half Routinery has drained a 100% battery. What about the other 17 hours of my working day I have routines set for those two and they aren’t things that can be run while my phone is plugged in just to conserve the battery required to use the app which reminds me what I’m supposed to be doing? I have very detailed twenty and thirty step routines over the course of two or three hours that I created— and mostly cannot even run on the app. Fix That and it’s a five star product. Improvement number two and this could just be nitpicky but the app for me glitches at least a half dozen times over the course of every day that I use— freezes the screen. I have to close the app and reopen it which takes half a minute sometimes. Actually a lot of times it takes me 30 seconds of trying to tap on the screen before I realize ‘oh it’s probably completely frozen and I need to shut it off and open it back up’. In a day we have 1440 minutes. I really dislike wasting five of them every day because of this smartphone glitch! it’s small annoyance but if you fix that and simultaneously double the price I would pay it and I suspect a lot of other people who are annoyed at the freezing Would happily do the same. Thirdly, there’s a setting somewhere in the apps software that is sending me a notification at 6 AM that says end of rest and another that says bedtime reminder at 11 PM. Neither of these is part of any of my routines that are currently activated. At least once per month I get so frustrated by this issue that I turn off all notifications for Routinery, just to stop those two notifications from waking me up when I am asleep. Please please make it easy to find inside the app where this can be turned off or tell me where it can be turned off if that setting already exists and my exhaustive search of the application has failed to find the setting!

title: Great app - frustrating sometimes though
body:
This is only way I’m able to start my day quickly. It’s a lifesaver! 

I’m struggling with it a bit lately though. I started a routine on my watch. I skipped some things, hoping they’d be added to the end—the watch doesn’t offer a choice of what to do when you skip like the phone does. 

After completing a couple of tasks, I needed to do the skipped tasks before moving on, but I couldn’t rearrange or do anything at all. Pretty normal for the watch app. I went to the phone app, and it says I have to end the watch routine and start it on the phone. I feel like they used to both run at the same time, which was really helpful. 

After ending the watch routine, I can’t unskip the skipped tasks on the phone. I can’t check them off either. They’re just.. crossed off for the day? I’m so confused as to why this is the way it’s working. If I don’t have full functionality on the watch, I should be able to switch to the phone quickly and easily and make whatever adjustment I need to, and then switch back to the watch. 

I used to start a routine on my watch and when I realized I needed to skip a task, I’d open up my phone and do it because I get to choose how to handle the skipped task as I’m skipping it. Then I’d just continue on the watch, no ending and restarting necessary. Now that the watch and phone app have been separated, I have to end the routine to make adjustments and that seems to be causing problems on top of being really inconvenient.

body: I am probably the person who has tried every schedule, routine, and self care app in the App Store. I recently started using Routinery’s free version, and I feel like an entirely new person! Because there’s room for error, the timer also helps me learn how long tasks take me, and will let me give myself enough time later! If I’ve overestimated how much time I need, then the routine gets done earlier! I’ve never been more productive in my LIFE and being without meds has always made things difficult. I have a streak of about three weeks and I feel so transformed… there is paid version option, but I don’t use it. It’s just become part of my morning ritual to set up my morning and afternoon routines! I love this app and 100% recommend it to anyone with motivation issues, you won’t burn out of this method, so give it a shot!!

title: Best routine app on the apps store
body:
Pros:

It’s really amazing all around, it allows you to save routines, then set alarms and shortcuts to start them. The countdown for each step is really nice for someone with ADHD and keeps me on task. The UX is cute and clean. There is a huge list of cool icons to use to represent each step and the routine as a whole (though those icons are seemingly randomly assigned as you create each step and you need to go back and correct them)

Missing features:

Missing a few features that could make things a little easier. You can’t easily add routines by copying and pasting them from outside the app. I have many routines saved in my notes app and I need to retype each step into Routinery to add them. Not too big an issue but still frustrating (especially since I have ADHD). Also, I’d love to be able to quick edit routines when I’m done with them in order to tweak and adjust them for further use. (Like adjusting the time for each step, adding steps I forgot, etc.)

I’ve also seen other apps use AI to quickly generate steps of a routine for you as a starting point. This could be a good “pro” feature addition down the line.

Overall, this is an incredible app that has been making my life much easier. Seriously, thank you so much for making this 😊✅

title: Helpful for ADHD
body: I have severe ADHD and haven’t had the best luck with medication, so I’m fully relying on coping skills and strategies to manage my symptoms. Initiating tasks, maintaining focus, and being aware of time passing are all things I struggle with a lot. And this app helps me with that. One of my routines is called “quick morning” for when I need to leave the house early, like for an 8am meeting. Watching the time tick down keeps me aware of how much time is passing, and how much time things are taking. Watching it tick down challenges me to be on time by racing the clock. I don’t need to panic trying to remember what to do because I’m following all of the necessary steps in order. And I’m less stressed about being late knowing that I’ll be ready at the end time of the routine. If you struggle with ADHD or any other time management or motivation issues, this is one of the few apps I’ve actually found helpful for more than like 3 days.

title: straight forward and easy to use
body:
i’ve developed these great routine blocks. I press play and it’s so easy for me to get through what I know I need to do. You can add time you can rearrange the order the day of you can also have it speak out certain things connect links if you’re a follow let’s say a YouTube warm-up video or there’s a form online that you need to use so I link certain websites for my workouts and I link certain YouTube videos for my daily stretches.

I have ADHD and this has been a lifesaver to get things done. I’ve tried so many apps, but this simple straightforward and easy to use program is my favorite and has worked the best for me. Their free version is great and the paid version is very affordable at under five dollars a month. I definitely recommend for anyone trying to be more consistent in their life bringing in better routine routines, or struggle with ADHD.

author: How time flies

title: This is the EFDD app you’re looking for
body:
It’s hard to overstate how good this app is. and this app is the only one that seems to get how Variable a day can be. 

The fact that you can:
- turn on and off notifications
- skip tasks
- reorder tasks
- +/- time to tasks
- see where your timeline
- set up context notes w/ links 
- set task to automatically jump or go-over
- check monthly/ weekly records of the tasks
- let routines run for hours 

 — basically means you can have a good or bad day without ever having to leave the app. And that is so important. 

 This app doesn’t orient itself around *should* but *is*. 

You can adjust everything mid routine OR NOT and because of this you can’t truly mess up your routine because the routine adjusts to you and your day. 

The learning curve isn’t steep and you can just download ones to start (like Bruce Lees!) 
But honestly the more you use this app the more you’re going to realize that your day is a series of routines. And the more you’re going to get done. 

Anyway I’ve tried a lot of EFDD/ADHD apps and this is the only one I’ve used everyday for years. It’s essential.

author: wfjeffries

title: This App Totally Changed My Day
body:
I’ve been using this app for about a month now, and it’s honestly amazing. I’ve tried so many apps, but this one actually works. It’s super easy to use, and the structure is just right—not too strict, but not too loose either. I love how you can pause or adjust routines if something unexpected comes up. It keeps me on track without making me feel stressed.
Before this, my mornings were a mess. Now I’ve got a simple routine that helps me start my day feeling productive. It’s wild how much better the rest of the day goes when you start off right. Even if I mess up or miss a step, it’s so easy to get back on track with this app.
I was worried it might feel too strict, but it doesn’t at all. It’s more like having a personal coach that helps you figure out what works for you. I’ve already customized my routines to fit my lifestyle, and it’s been a huge help.
If you’re new to routines, start small! Just set up one simple routine and see how it feels. That’s what I did, and now I can’t imagine my day without it. Honestly, it’s one of the best apps I’ve ever used for staying organized and building better habits.
Highly recommend if you’re looking to manage your time better or just feel more in control of your day. Totally worth it!

title: Strange, Depressing App
body: Routinery is an app for people who lack the self control to use a standard time-blocking app. As someone with intense ADHD, I thought the structure this app provides would be helpful. Instead, after using Routinery, I found myself more bound to the unnatural rigidness of tech than I ever thought I’d be. Meaning, the structure this app encourages is at odds with human lifestyles. Beyond including a pause button, it doesn’t offer the ability to handle variance in your life. It insists on a structure that you feel bound to, as if an overbearing boss strapped a tracking device to your hand and asked that you manage your time according to the needs of the business. Sure, you are in control of your needs with this app, you designate how you spend your time. Though, I could see a negative psychological response for many who use this app as for those of us with severe focus issues, straying from the structure of time this app demands could become stressful and therefore discouraging. It did for me. I highly recommend a standard time-blocking method and encouraging yourself to stick to the structure through reminders and in others ways that are unique to your needs. Also, the Dwayne Johnson and Kim Kardashian routine examples are cringey and odd to incorporate into an app. The experience for me has been a bit depressing. It allowed for technology to become far too heavy of a hand in my routine and I’m happy I no longer use it.

title: Incredible life changer in its simplicity!
body:
Thank you, thank you, thank you for this app! It has been a game changer for my mornings, and is so wonderfully simple that my mind doesn’t feel overwhelmed by the design. I don’t need charts, just a simple app for use when I gotta get moving in short spurts, and this is the only app I’ve found that does this so well. It’s the first time I’ve had huge success cultivating a morning routine as an adult.

I love how practical the customization is for each step, such as the choice to auto-next or not. The ETA for the routine’s end is gold for keeping me on task and hustling, fun emojis, just an overall great interface and options during the routine.

 I do wish you had the option to edit notification sounds or auto-next for a whole routine in one step, but this app is so helpful I don’t mind. It does make things a little tedious though when setting up. But the level of customization means that I can find out what works for me through doing the routine for a few days until it’s fine tuned.

Lastly, thank you to the developers for adding apple watch support and actively working on this app together. This has been such a gift in my life and growth, keep going!

title: Seems great, what's with the battery drain?
body:
Like the app a lot, I am a premium user. Very useful for establishing habits.

But if I leave Routinery on my iPad Pro m1, it will drain the entire full battery in a matter of a couple of hours! There is no sound playing, it's just the basic screen.

iOS reports Routinery as using over 90% of my battery each day. Something is up.

My other issue: you cannot sync routines between devices when they're running! I will open my phone to continue a routine I'm running, and it will not show any progress unless I stop the routine on the other device, then I can continue.

These two things are almost dealbreakers for an otherwise great app, especially how the second one makes the first worst, since I can't swap between devices to save my poor battery.

title: Must Pay for Full Usability
body:
I am looking for a habit-tracking app that is easy to use, doesn't require a subscription, and doesn't force you to watch advertisements.

Unfortunately, this application requires about $4/month. Some of the features that are locked for only subscribed users are custom reminder sounds, an ad-free experience, and satisfaction notes (recording your feelings). 

I like that this application asked me about my demographics and preferences so it could tailor the routine. I also liked that once the routine was created, I was able to adjust things like the time associated with the task. It is nice that the routine starts off with a quick breathing exercise. This application is ultimately not for me because I’m looking for something where I can actually analyze my data and discover patterns, which won’t be possible without paying.

title: Changed my life the first day!!

Normally I would spend my day planning my day but not end up with any time left to actually do anything I planned lol! I was always running late and never felt like I had enough time for anything! I didn’t even realized how distracted I was! I’d go to start laundry but then notice the bathroom needs to be cleaned so I’d start that and then notice the floors need to be swept so I’d jump to that and I’d try doing a million things at once stressing about time for all the other things and now I can just focus on one thing at a time because I know that everything is in my routine so I’ll get to those things at their time and don’t need to worry! I feel so at peace and so at ease now! I even schedule in stretching and meditation which I always tricked myself into thinking I didn’t have time for! At the end of my day i feel so energized and accomplished and I’m shocked that it’s so easy to keep up on all the chores and to prioritize self care at the same time! I never have laundry or dishes sitting for days… and I get everything done so fast and then I have so much free time and can actually enjoy it! I usually just felt super busy all day but would somehow not get anything done! I’m so thrilled that it’s only $2/ month to feel like I normal human! 😂

author: Atticus Steven Parker

title: Not a lot of bells & whistles for the price
body:
I’m updating my review here, because I’ve figured out all of the issues that I was having. The main issue with the text to speech can be turned off only while the routine is running. In day view, it’s grey and difficult to see, but it is there and it fixed my problem. I use this app everyday now, and it helps me focus on what’s important, so I do recommend it. The syncing is working great now, and the lagging only seemed to occur when I created my routines. So, I’m changing my review from 4 to 5 stars.

Old review:
Unlike many who have complained, I actually did subscribe to the annual subscription, and I get that the goal here is simplicity. But, simple design does not mean less features / functionality. The huge disappointment for me is that you can’t turn off the text-to-speech when a task runs over! I listen to audiobooks during my morning routine and I guess I’m going to have to run this on my iPad in the bathroom while my phone plays my audio, because there is no way to keep it from interrupting. If I had realized this before subscribing, I would not have subscribed. But, there aren’t really any other apps like this. In the past, I used apps like Seconds and MyIntervals, which are for creating workouts. They have way more options within each routine, and I don’t care about summaries or tracking overall progress. I do not have ADHD, nor am I neurodivergent - I just like to be organized. I do have depression and productivity apps help motivate me and keep me focused, so I do rely on them. I turned off the chatbot, which was annoying, and I’m glad that option was available, but there need to be more ways to customize. And, I agree that that the lag times are perplexing. When scrolling, it often freezes and you have to wait for it to “think”. I turned off all the automatic switches from one task to the next (took forever to do because of lag), hoping it would stop talking, but with no luck. It literally announces that the last task has ended automatically, in full, and that the next task has started, in full. Then, it keep nagging every minute over or so, too, even if I pause the routine! I have all routines set to silent with no automatic tasks and I cannot believe the text-to-speech is still so disruptive. I don’t even want it to beep - I just want to check the task when I’m done. I guess I can go make all the tasks way longer so I always complete the task within the timeframe, but I kind of wanted something with close to accurate times to push me - that was the point. Then, I guess I can just stop the routine if I need to stop to do something else for a few minutes, but how inconvenient, and who knows if it’s going to work properly, like save my previous tasks. It seems like whoever made this had a particular goal or vision , which is good, but the code and technical design needs work. I will say that it’s pretty reliable if the app gets closed or exited or anything, about keeping the time going. Any edits to routines get synced well to iCloud, but it doesn’t always sync daily progress between devices.

author: Neptunebound

title: Great features but needs improvements to be worth the money.
body:
Pros:
-screen stays on while app is open, with a countdown for each activity
-notification sounds at 1 min before activity ends, and at end (you can change this, and decide whether to automatically or manually switch tasks)
-voice that tells you to switch activities (helpful if you can’t be looking at the screen at all times)
 -ability to skip an activity for the day (during or before routine starts)

Other routine apps have been missing these features, which are essential for this to be effective for me.

However… cons:
-app sends you banner notifications between activities even when app is open and not in the background
-primary issue—you can only do a routine once per day, and you cannot adjust a routine you’re going to do tomorrow if you have already done it today. Especially in free version this is extremely frustrating as I need to change my routine depending on the day and how much time I have.
-secondary issue—sound is a bit of a mess. You can adjust with phone volume, but the app volume will randomly shoot way up and start shouting at you, which in addition to scaring me can also be heard by the neighboring apt.
-the voice sometimes calls out the wrong activity
-no connection to a calendar/schedule as some other apps have, this is helpful

 Overall, I’d like more than just the 2 free routines, but can’t justify that price without some changes being made to these issues—ESPECIALLY since you have to pay that price on a recurring basis!

title: Amazing app for staying present, especially with ADHD
body: Ever since I started using this app, I feel so regulated and content. The timers help me focus on one task at a time and not get sidetracked, so I’m able to feel calmer and less overwhelmed by everything there is to do. I know that the app will tell me what to do next, so I don’t need to keep reminding myself of all the things I need to do. I never have to dig into my brain to make sure I remembered to do everything (and make sure I do everything in the right order, stay on track, remember what to do next, etc.). At first I thought the timers would stress me out, but they actually just force me to surrender and do the task at hand — and it gives me a sense of pride when I finish something early/on time. When I get ready for the day and unwind from the day, I can let go of all my thoughts, worries, and tension, and just be. This calmness and stability carries over to the rest of my day and to my night of sleep. Thank you for this beautiful app and I highly recommend to anyone <3

title: Please make this a one-time purchase instead of a subscription!
body:
This would be a five-star review except that I will probably always be stuck using the free version (which limits you to two routines) because I am unwilling to pay a monthly fee for something that should be a one-time purchase.

This app has been a game-changer for my ADHD, hugely helpful for getting me out the door to work mostly on time in the morning and helping me wind down for bedtime in a timely manner. I took a year off from using Routinery in 2023 because I had a baby and wasn’t working, and my routines kept changing as my baby grew. Now, in 2024, I’m going back to work (and also now having to get my daughter off to daycare!) so I’m back! I was disappointed to discover that, in addition to limiting the user to two routines, the free version now apparently has ads??? I would love to make a one-time purchase in order to unlock the premium features of this app, but really, really don’t want to pay $27 per year (or $95 per year at full price!)

I understand the philosophy of routines that build habits like this but I need to also be able to check things off my todo list without starting a timer and going through things in sequence. I need more flexibility. A dumb mode where I can just check off what I’ve already done and look over what’s left etc very quickly. I’m not a robot I do things at different times, for different durations and in different orders but I still need something to keep me on track with daily repeating todos and reminders. I find myself wrestling with this app. Would work if I could just add tasks without durations and complete them without starting the timer.

title: Updated: Recent Changes Unfortunate
body:
Edit: I realized to ask for more clarification from the creators at a later time, as it sounded like I was unable to easily edit the app due to a fixable bug. Apparently, this is no longer a feature. I had to stop using the app while my subscription was going as this was its most important feature for me. I can't find an app that is easy to edit and use but has some variety. I would think this would be important for many neurodivergent people, but apparently, I am an outlier even amongst them, which is incredibly discouraging. We barely have niche markets anymore. So it's very depressing to assume that as technology progresses, accessibility will likely decrease, even though in theory it should improve.

Previous Review:

Note: might change the rating at some point (was four, now is three, in theory it is closer to five). I used to use this app every day, but one of my favorite aspects—which is essential for me in any app like this—was the ability to edit my routine on the go. And the app makers are friendly and responsive. The latest update makes reordering easier, but no longer allows one to change the name of any of the tasks at hand. I’ve been testing it after each update to see if it’s changed. So far, no dice. Another significant issues are that it drains a LOT of battery and messes with the audio on my phone to the point that it will blast your ears out lol. This is frankly more of an iPhone problem than just this app (iPhone refuses to acknowledge this, in spite of LOTS of evidence; presumably it’ll cost them less to get sued by those with ear damage than to make the change), but it does depend on the app to an extent. Taking a break from this app has helped my battery and ears a lot. It’s possible the latest updates have also addressed that as they now have volume levels in the app. Anyway, I’m a bit sad to stop using it, but I might end up having to delete. Otherwise, it’s a very fun, cute, and flexible app.

title: Routines are great, Premium not so much
body:
The routine creation and interface are very functional from a user perspective.

However, the restriction on the number of routines for free users is almost ridiculous considering the apps subscription based premium access. There is zero desire from a user perspective to continuously pay for access to more routines, as there is no guarantee that the prices won’t increase over time, and the overall shift towards subscription based services is already too much. A one time payment for premium is justifiable - but not a subscription. Users deserve to own premium rather than pay for access to it.

I have had the app for more than a year and will never buy premium if it continues to be a subscription service. If it were available as a one time purchase, I would buy premium immediately.
author: fair_sophia

title: Very good
body:
I find this really helpful for my morning routine. I have it setup with Shortcuts so that when I disconnect from charging in the morning, it starts the routine.

It keeps me from forgetting things or getting too distracted. Also helps to do things I may feel lazy about. Since you’re kind of turning your brain off and doing what it says, you’re more likely to just do it instead of talking yourself out of it.

Also in that spirit, I make the early tasks very simple while I’m still sleepy. Literally “get out of bed”, “open the blinds”, “put on workout clothes”, “go downstairs”, etc. Then I have more general tasks with bigger blocks of time later on.

Since it estimates when you’ll be done, it helps to keep things in balance. If I see I’m running late and my routine will go past the start of my first work meeting, I can do a shorter meditation or exercise session, instead of suddenly noticing the time and having to rush around.

There’s been bugs in the past (like the voice repeating or the timer not showing up on the dynamic island & Lock Screen), but those big ones have been fixed. The voice is pretty robotic and I didn’t like it at first, but it also makes me want to finish on time to avoid hearing it lol.

Sometimes I wish you could link routines or put routines inside other routines so you could more easily have variations on diff days or move multiple tasks around at once, but I’m not sure there’d be a way to do it without making things too complicated. It works well enough most of the time now anyway.

title: The app you can’t live without after trying
body:
If you’ve ever read the book “what the most successful people do before breakfast,” then you’re aware of the concept of writing every task down that you want accomplished, about how long each task takes, and what time you want to have it completed. I went from “tracking” on a notepad to randomly finding this in the App Store one day looking for if there was a better way for me to do it. 

Gamechanger, life saver, I can’t get through my mornings without it. 

I thought making my bagel took me 1 minute- nope, about 2 minutes to toast, the time it takes to get the jam and a knife out, and to put said knife in the dishwasher- I’m looking at 5 minutes for a bagel. May be a dumb example, but this app not only holds you to the times set for yourself, it makes you well aware of how much time you ACTUALLY take to accomplish a task. 

My morning routine starts with simply get out of bed, make bed, bathroom, etc, etc, and ends with how long my route to work is. If I want to be at work by 730? Then guess what- I’m leaving at 717, not in shambles running out the door at 725 in hopes I make it on time. Nope, because I have a tracker that is keeping tabs on me and I’m therefore keeping tabs on myself. 

Get this app. Just do it. It will completely change the way you tackle your mornings and nights and days

title: Best Routine App!
body: Words aren’t adequate enough to describe how much I adore this app. I tried a bunch of productivity/routine apps, but this was the best one!! I used to struggle so much with getting ready in the morning and before bed, but this app has seriously fixed most of my problems with that. While I will admit it only lets you have two free routines, the free version of this app is actually still amazing!!! Even without premium, you can have your routines as long as you want and set exactly how long each task is. It also lets you rearrange things as you go if your routine doesn’t go as planned/needs to be altered. And one of the best features is how a voice reads out when your current task is finished and tells you what the next one is! It also warns you when you only have a minute left if the task is a longer one. Even when you don’t have the app pulled up on your phone, it continues to run in the background and sends you alerts throughout your routine! I recommend this for ANYONE who finds it hard to keep track of routines, especially if you’re neurodivergent like I am!!

author: AstroKnight610

title: Frustrating Bugs!
body:
EDIT: 
Updating my review as many of the bugs and glitches mentioned in the previous review, which I'll leave down below, have been addressed, though sometimes they still occur, which is why I'm leaving my initial review.
However, after reading through many of the other reviews, I find that I agree with one consistent complaint, aside from the bugs: the subscription-based pay system. I would buy this app in a heartbeat, if it were a one time fee, as opposed to being a reoccurring subscription.
I also find that they words things in a way where it is easy for people to misunderstand exactly what they are buying. For example, it is currently in the middle of January 2023, and they are running a sale for New Year's Day. Right now, it said that I can buy a one-month, three-month, or yearly subscription at a discount and also receive an additional code for the same amount of time. So basically, if I bought the yearly subscription, I would get a code that would cover a subscription for an additional year--2 years total. I
 almost bought this in a heartbeat, but I am glad that I waited. In very small fine print (that is a light gray text color against a white background, so barely visible) it states that the code cannot be used for yourself, but must be given to someone else so that you can "gift" Routinery to a loved one. Personally, I find this very sneaky and deceiving. 
Every time I decide that I would like to subscribe to the app--because it actually has helped me a lot whenever I use the two routines that come with the free version--the developer makes me change my mind by either being slow to fix bugs that have been reported and complained about for months, or they pull deceptive tricks in order to get money.
To the developer, I suggest you heed the advice of your users and either adjust the pay system, or consider lowering the fee, seeing as it is taking months, and sometimes even over a year for certain bugs to be fixed. From what I am gathering, it sounds like either a single person or a very small team is working on this app, so I completely understand not being able to keep up with requests and fixing bugs in a fast manner, but the price for the app paired with the bugs are not a good match.
 
-------------
Original Review
The premise of this app is a great one, but there are so many bugs that this feels like a beta version of the app instead of a full release. I cannot select any icons at all (except for those in the “morning“ page) to assign to a task. In order to be able to select any other icons in their icon library, I have to click “randomize” until I happen to fall on an icon that relates to the task that I’m inputting. I even tried deleting the entire app to see if the download had simply glitched out, but the problem persists. It’s extremely frustrating to try to add a task when it takes five minutes of pressing the randomize icon button and hoping that you happen upon an icon that’s somewhat related to your task. And this is with the trial version of the paid subscription. I honestly am surprised that they are charging money for this whenever the app is so broken. I think the app could use a great deal of fixing before it is released to the public. As it stands right now, the app is so glitchy, it crashes and loses my progress constantly. I hate it because honestly, this is the one system that I found that actually seemed to work for me; initially, when I followed the tutorial and created a morning routine, it worked out great. However, the bugs quickly showed up soon after. Developers, has this bug for the icons and the inability to select specific icon categories or even specific icons themselves been noted before? And if so, is there a fix coming soon? I really want to like this app, but so far, the bugs are making it really hard to do so. Edit: lowering my review to one star based on customer “support.” I emailed the developers about several bugs I am experiencing and was told simply to make sure I was upgraded to the latest version. I told them this information already as I stated in my first email I even deleted the app and re-downloaded in an attempt to fix the problem, but the problems persisted. They still have not contacted back after that single, very unhelpful reply. Scrolling through the reviews, it seems like everyone is complaining about the same bugs, some even from a year ago. And it doesn’t look like the developer(s) are listening. I love the idea of this app, but the support from the developer is severely lacking. I planned to buy the subscription but will be looking elsewhere for an app that is more properly managed. If anyone has any suggestions, I’d love if you would leave them in your review to check them out! UPDATE: The bugs mentioned in the initial review have since been fixed, but now, a new major bug has taken their place. When starting a routine, the screen suddenly goes completely white except for the top half where it displays part of the screen. Then the routine begins, but it cuts to the last task. Ending the routine and restarting it usually helps, but I noticed after that occurs, each timed task suddenly randomly completes itself. For example, I have a morning routine and it will be on a task like “get dressed” which is set to last for 2 minutes, but the timer makes the “complete” sound after it has only run for maybe 15 seconds and it jumps to the very next task.

title: THE ONLY APP THAT HELPS (2 months daily use)
body: I scoured the App Store for routine supporting apps. When I found a well-reviewed app that met the criteria I had in mind, I put in hours of testing. I ended up trying out Structured, Habit Hub, Tiimo, Brili Routines, & Time Bloc. Tiimo came the closest to the functionality of Routinery, but it was so glitchy it was unusable.   I’ve been using this app for 2 months so far. It is SO HELPFUL for my executive function issues (late-diagnosed adult ADHD and ASD). Routinery offers the ability to build what I call “routine playlists” (abbreviated as rp henceforth). Some of the apps I tested also have this function. Routinery’s playlists are unique because: 1))) each task in the rp is assigned a duration & when the rp runs each task has a timer (essential for me, because I have time-blindness), 2))) rps & individual tasks can be aperiodic (free from scheduling) OR scheduled, 3))) when an rp is running, tasks *do not* autocomplete until I press the ✅ (unless I select the “auto-next” setting for that specific task), 4))) audio & voice notifications are available at a variety of intervals to indicate the beginning, time remaining, and end of a task, as well as a stopwatch count of time elapsed since the anticipated task completion point if I’ve gone over time on a task and time elapsed since rp was paused (so useful because I often get distracted & completely forget I’ve paused an rp), 5))) creating, skipping & reordering tasks is much quicker & simpler than other apps I tested.

title: A winner for my neurodivergent brain
body:
I used Tiimo before but wasn’t super happy with it (personal preferences). I also had issues with it working consistently with my Apple Watch. After downloading and deleting several other routine apps I found Routinery. It has been fantastic. 

 *Things I like:*

-  It has a clean and minimalistic design. It clicked with my brain right away 
- Creating a new routine is a quick and easy process You can update an existing routine without any excess steps 
- Everything is clearly labeled
- The font and buttons are large enough to navigate with ease 
- You are able to duplicate a routine. This is handy for me when my routine changes by one activity on a given day. For example, on Sundays my closing duties routine is the same but with the addition of filling my pillbox for the upcoming week. It's nice to not have to create a whole new routine from scratch
- There are a variety of settings to make it customized to my needs - timer settings, settings for improved concentration, and add-ons like haptic vibration and status bar
- There is a timer setting under Push Notifications called "Pause Timer Notification" that you can turn on. If it's on it will notify you 5, 10, and/or 20 minutes after you pause an activity in a routine to remind you that it's paused 
- There's an option to not automatically go to the next activity(!!!) 
- It has worked seamlessly with my Apple Watch thus far which is a must for me 

*Things I dislike:*  
- I'd like the option to view individual days rather than just Today 

Clearly a winner for me!

For example, I’d like to set a routine for packing a bag to work remotely at the park. The items in the bag are consistent and Routinery would help me get it done quickly, not forgetting anything, but I don’t need this routine at a consistent time every week. The same goes for certain work out routines. I’m also a dog sitter and my routine changes when I’m getting up super early to walk dogs, but that only lasts for about a week at a time. The point is that temporary routines can be useful.
I am already loving this app and I use it for my regular morning and evening routines. I just think adding the option to use certain routines at irregular times would make it even better.

title: Best Routine App Available!!
body: I love this app! I love the structure, I love the imagery. I love that it tracks streaks, I love that it reminds you and even has a voice reminder when ur looking away from your phone. I like the interface, it’s the BEST compared to a lot of other routine apps. As someone who’s struggling to follow their paper planner and paper written routines, having it visible on the phone with a timer and an estimated finishing time has been so helpful. I’ve been able to properly gauge how much time I have left to do things and whether I have to skip a task etc. it’s been helping me with establishing a solid routine for myself. I love it. However, there’s one thing that I don’t love. I don’t love that it’s a subscription. For this kind of app, I feel like a subscription is kinda… bogus. I understand that creators want to be compensated for their work, but ever since every service shifted to subscriptions it’s been a pain to even think about adding one. It seems so cheap at first, but add the cost of your streaming services(Netflix, Hulu, Spotify), business services(Microsoft, trello,wix, etc.), other apps(Apple +, Fitbit +, etc), tangible services(gym memberships, dance lessons, piano lessons etc.) . It’s like everyone wants to make MORE money these days for services that should have a FLAT COST and it’s getting ridiculous. I mean how can all these creators expect us to hold all these different subscriptions? I will say, the subscription is CHEAP and that’s nice. But if I’m being honest, I don’t think it’s a service worth subscribing to. At that point I’d rather retry the pen and paper and see how far I get. However, I DO think that it deserves compensation. That’s actually what I was preparing to do before writing this review. I think that the app needs to have an option for a FLAT COST that allows the user to buy access to all the features for lifetime. If you were giving me LIFETIME access to the features, I’d be willing to go up to maybe $60 just to be able to get ALL the features for a lifetime because this app has really helped me.  Some people prefer subscriptions and will pay, but for those of us that don’t see a point in subscribing to an app with basic but helpful functions(or those who already have too many subscriptions), please give us a FLAT COST that allows us to compensate you in the method we may best see fit. Thank you

I love it because you can allot the amount of time that tasks take you (a best guess is fine bc you can see how much time that task usually takes you over a few weeks and adjust it accordingly so it’s accurate) and then seeing everything together, you know exactly when you will be finished with the routine, so you don’t have to be stressed like “oh I don’t have time to do all these things” because you know you have time for it!

author: trxndn

title: Life-changing
body:
I’ve always struggled getting out the door on time for appointments, work, anything really. Part of ADHD is time perception dysfunction. We literally perceive time differently and have difficulty judging how long it actually takes to do things or knowing how much time has passed while performing a task. 

The app Routinery (iPhone) was a game changer for me. You create a routine (e.g. “Get ready for work”), and break it down into individual tasks. Then you put them in order and assign an amount of time for each. When you “run” the routine, your phone buzzes and prompts you each step of the way, and also updates your estimated end time based on how long it takes you to actually perform each task. So my AM routine literally starts with “take pills - 1 min” and then “stretch - 2 min”. Shower is next, and if I want to skip it because I showered the night before, then I skip it and it prompts me to do the next task which also updates the expected end time to show I’ll be done early. So maybe I end up taking a little longer to do my “makeup - 10 min” task. It buzzes that my time is up, but continues running the clock so I can see a) how much time I’m going over the expected time, and b) that I will still be done with my routine by whatever o’clock or that I will be late if I don’t skip something else later in the routine. 

I have been amaaaazed at how quickly I can actually do certain things when I am not constantly distracted by multitasking, and also not constantly checking my clock because I’m convinced that I’m going to be late if I don’t pay attention to the time. So it has allowed me to actually take time for meditation or checking emails or spending more time on my makeup, etc because I know for sure that I’ll be able to leave on time and I’m not just guessing. 

The other major use I have for it is a few routines I call “day off chores” and “deep clean”, etc. I created routines where I not only list tasks to do, but also include prep or transition time. Also, by deciding on a logical order of tasks ahead of time, I don’t get stuck in the never ending wheel of no accomplishment that ADHDers are famous for. Example: cleaning the bathroom. One task is just gathering rugs and towels and putting them in the wash. Then, scrubbing the toilet because the cleaner can soak in the bowl for a bit while I do the next thing. I have a task just for taking things off the bathroom counter, before the next task of wiping the counter and sink. It continues like this and it seems crazy but it ensures that I don’t get distracted and the most amazing thing is realizing that after programming a whole routine and adding the times I expect each task to take, the actual time is so much less than I assumed it would take. Before, sometimes cleaning the bathroom ends up being an all-day journey and for that reason I justify avoiding doing it. But if I know that I can deep clean my bathroom in about 20 min, it suddenly becomes super possible and satisfying. 

My day off routine includes things like “take a walk - 20 min” and “drink water” interspersed with productive tasks. It’s incredible how often I convince myself that I’m don’t have time to do things for myself and my mental health because im too busy. But by programming it into the routine, not only am I not worried about losing focus and getting back to productivity, but I don’t feel guilty about having “me time” because it’s considered just another task and I know I can fit it into the time I have. 

It is free to download but there is a price to use the app.  I think you can try it free for a time and then pay monthly, or annually. But honestly, about $20 for a year of life-changing task-prompting is worth it to me. 

Alllllllso, it’s notifications sync to my Fitbit so I don’t need to worry about having my phone in front of me and getting distracted while I’m going through my tasks. Just another thing that makes it awesome. 

Best of luck to you!

title: A great app for me, despite the bugs
body:
I have ADHD that I would say falls somewhere between “inconvenient” and “crippling.” Part of living with ADHD is figuring out what one is bad at, and personally I am bad at keeping lists of things in my head. So to keep things running at home, I have to-do routines that I do every morning. I used to use the Productive app for this, but the more cutesy that app got the more it distracted me. (I don’t need to be reminded to drink water, I need an app that yells at me until I do the dishes.) I searched around and found Routinery, and I think it’s very good at what it does. Its UI is simple, perhaps a little unconventional for an iOS app, but it does what it says on the tin, and that’s what matters. 

My only reservations about recommending this to others lie in the fact that the app is buggy on my 12” iPad. Sometimes it will spin forever while opening, and sometimes it will crash out of nowhere. However, the devs have been very good at ensuring my to-do list doesn’t lose progress, even if there is a crash. These are the kinds of failures that a dev can fix (I used to write apps, a long time ago) so I’m sure they will be fixed in the future. In the meantime, this app is very helpful in keeping me in sync with my chores and responsibilities.
author: patrickthmsn

title: OUTSTANDING! Best of its kind.
body:
Dozens of productivity apps have failed me before I found Routinery. Most productivity apps actually make us less productive because they require the user to exercise perfect judgment when making scheduling decisions. Those apps make it too easy to feel good in the moment when we create a new task... but those apps fail to account for the fact that people often don't do what they say they are going to do. On stressful or lazy days I ended up doing what was most convenient. 

Routinery is the ONLY app that has worked for me because it is convenient! The UI/UX reduces the amount of effort required to create a new routine. It lessens the barriers between activites I want to do more often by making it more convenient for me to start them and do them.I noticed improvements right away!

Routinery is the only productivity app with a "Recommended Routines" feature. There are a few dozen curated routines for Morning, Afternoon, Night, Productivity, Famous People's Routines, etc.It's so easy to just start from one of these (instead of having to spend an hour coming up with a routine on my own, I'd much rather start from popular examples). if you want to start a new routine you can also use their templates of individual tasks. The individual task templates also correspond to a specific time which is SOOO convenient. (So I don't have to think about each and every task and ask myself, how much time does it take me to do this?)

With previous to-do apps, I used to spend a couple of hours writing down my vision for a brand new routine. After wasting all that time, I would feel overwhelmed by the amount of effort required to settle into my new schedule... and I couldn't even manage to start. Delete the schedule, delete the app, download another, and start the maddening cycle all over again. Those days are gone, thanks to Routinery!

author: I liked it few days ago but

title: Huge potential; nagging issues
body:
This app is a great idea, has many well thought out features, and I can see it being an indispensable part of my life. I bought premium immediately. By far the best way to use it is with Apple Watch, though the phone app is absolutely necessary for designing the routines. 

Major issues:
- Any music playing stops when you start a routine on the phone app
- Apple Watch app sends THREE loud notifications when you need to switch tasks, two overlapping each other and one with a totally different sound. It sounds rather bad!
- Apple Watch app has sync issues. Oftentimes in the morning will show all my routines as completed, sometimes gets stuck in a weird state

Love:
- Estimated end time on routines. I struggle with time blindness and it blows my mind every day that my morning routine takes 20 minutes even though each action is under two minutes. 
- Records of start and end times of routines, and how much over or under you were on each task, for every routine you’ve ever completed.
- Attractive UI. 
- Clear explanations for what most settings do.
- Tasks you add are saved, so you can add the same task to other routines with one click. 
- Timer effect on each task (if you’ve used the physical time timer, it’s like that)
- notes and feedback on routines (so you can remember what you want to change later)
- repeated notifications are available if you’ve gone over time on a task or paused it. Indispensable if you get distracted easily 
- suggested routines (find them under “Explore” when adding a new routine)
- home screen widgets available 

Top suggestions for quality of life improvements:
- Faster options for moving a task to the end of a routine. For example, swipe up on the task card to send it to the end. Right now this requires 2-3 clicks. 
- Icon search when adding icons to tasks (or option to use regular emojis as the icon, since iOS keyboard has search built in)
- More obvious/colorful full timer effect on tasks, so the disappearing timer is easily visible from farther away

author: shgmc

title: Weight check?
body: I started setting up my morning routine and one of the suggested activities is a weight check, saying “check your weight changes daily.” I did this for years and it is extremely psychologically damaging, to anyone. This can caused disordered eating & obsessive behaviors that are never healthy. For an app advertised to people with ADHD, this is dangerous and can cause fixation. ADHDers are prone to disordered eating already, from food fixations, forgetting to eat, meds killing appetite, executive dysfunction when it comes to cooking, etc. It takes a long time for a lot of us to hack these things and learn to feed our bodies, and fixating on daily weight changes can be so destructive to our mental and physical health. Weight≠health

title: Love (life changing), have some suggestions!
body:
I have ADHD and autism, so I always struggle with routine and organization, but also crave it and need it to function.

This app has made it possible for me to get out of bed on time in the morning, even if I’m tired. Why? Because the daily struggle and stress of trying to remember everything and the shame when I inevitably can’t or am late… is just GONE. I don’t have to use my brain right away, or stress out about forgetting anything, or decide what to do next. I’m not rushing. Even the boring stuff is easy. It’s easy to change the order of habits to optimize.

Also, the time tracking report (green/red with time differences) of individual habits for each completed routine is done very well, and is a GODSEND for my time blindness (I have no innate sense of time, and my house is covered with timers because of this.)

I’m rating this 5 stars because it is much better than anything else I’ve tried, and I love using it. It’s changing my life for the better. 

I do have a few suggestions:

1. Please add an option for unlimited reminders to start the next task! For those of us with ADHD, 5 is actually not enough. It’s easy to get absorbed in something and tune out the alarm, and then when all 5 go by I forget I was doing a routine. 

2. Please add an option for anytime-routines! Some routines are not planned at a specific time.

3. Please add an option to pause routines and have multiple on hold, or implement sub-routines that can be added to other routines! For example, one habit in my nighttime routine is to pack lunch for the next day, but sometimes I do that in the morning. I’d like to pause my main routine, go through the packing steps routine, and then finish that and continue with my main one. Not sure about the best way to make that work.

4. The icons are beautiful, but also not easy to navigate - the categories are a little arbitrary. It would be awesome if you could search for them using keywords or tags. I spend a LOT of time searching for an appropriate icon for each habit, which is time better spent creating the routine, and makes it harder for me to want to create new routines. Even easier would be an option to use an emoji as an icon, but the icons are beautiful, and I do love them. 

5. It would be nice to have an easy way to submit a request for a missing icon! For example, I would love a few different bags (duffel for gym, backpack, purse), as I spend a lot of time each day packing that stuff. An icon for “unpacking” would be amazing too. Or just the option to use emojis.

6. The time tracking summary after each routine is BEAUTIFUL, and it helps me so much. I wish there was a way to easily use the recorded time differences to update habit durations without having to switch screens so I could better learn how long individual things really take me. Writing them all down and then updating each habit in each routine individually is too much for me. 

7. Kinda related to 6: The same habits in different routines can have different duration settings (it’s like they are separate copies.) I wish there was a way to update the icons or durations of all copies at once from the original, or maybe have a way to apply it to all and de-select some, or have an option to enable or disable each habit added to a routine to sync updates from the original. 

8. An interactive tutorial would be great! I think I’m probably still missing things. 

Don’t take these suggestions as a reason not to use the app - it rocks!!! I’m a software developer so I just do this naturally, I can find problems with anything! I’m so grateful to the developers ❤️
