title: My life is worse without Routinery
body:
Routinery revolutionized my morning and evening routines. This app is a timer. You list a sequence of tasks you need to do and how long each of the subtasks take. You start the timer, and the app displays one task on the screen. Press the check mark to move on to the next subtask. This app takes all the guess work out of everything. You focus on nothing but the task. And the timer reassures you that doing that dreaded chore does not actually take forever. 

I actually had stopped using this app for a few weeks. Editing the task was very confusing and cumbersome. But I will give this app another chance because I have to. I don’t think I can afford to not use this app. My quality of life has been noticeably worse without it.

If anyone is overwhelmed by using this app, I would start off by listing out every little thing. Once you develop good habits, you don’t need to keep everything anymore, maybe only the things you tend to avoid. 

As for feedback for the app, I still think the editing process needs some work. There’s a mode where you can change the order or delete, but you can’t edit the content of the task. That doesn’t make sense to my brain. Tapping the task should let me edit the contents, and a little “handle” at the end of the box can change the task order.

I don’t really use the contexts and feedback. It doesn’t make sense to me what they’re for because I can’t see the text when I’m in the middle of the routine. It could be useful if I could write a short sentence so I could read it while in the middle of the routine. But I can’t. 

Also, the motivational words at the top are a little weird sounding, like a non-native speaker of English. But this complaint doesn’t have to do with the function of the app, which is the most important thing.

Also lots of reviews talk about the app crashing. I have literally NEVER EVER had this problem.

As I start using this app again, I’ll update this review with more of my thoughts. I am just so passionate and grateful for this app. Everyone knows that not every product compels people to rave review it.

title: iOS app great! Watch app won’t even open
body:
UPDATE: Watch app works now, although it seems things still get out of sync, and sometimes iOS app won’t open.

UPDATE #2: After updating some routines, watch app got out of sync again! Reinstalled watch app and now getting dreaded “Please open Routinery app on your iPhone”. This app is too unreliable for me considering I rely on the watch to run my routines.

——

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

First of all, I would like to say that the iOS app is fantastic and works very well to help you build habits and routines. That being said, the watch app has gone from finicky to working half the time to not even opening at all anymore which is *truly* disappointing.

I used to use the watch app independently of the phone, and it had some major syncing issues (usually one device lagging behind and then overriding the other’s progress), but it at least worked for the most part without having to open the phone app. This was helpful for those who want to eg avoid the distractions on their phone.

Then the watch app was changed to rely on the iOS app being opened first. I guess this was to fix the syncing issues, but it totally killed the ability to leave the phone behind and use only the watch, and wouldn’t work half the time without 1) starting a routine on the phone and 2) skipping/finishing some habits on the iOS app. Imagine the frustration when you have several routines.

Now the watch app crashes on startup regardless of the state of the iOS app. Basically, you can’t open it. It’s completely broken!

Even if the watch app is fixed so that it stops crashing, the fact that you must open the iOS app first (and start a routine on it) makes a watch-centered experience a distant dream, which is a real pity since it was mostly working before. I thought I had found my endgame routine app, but no longer. 🙁

iOS = great 
watchOS = currently 🗑🔥

title: Genuinely life-changing!
body:
I have ADHD (primarily inattentive type) and it used to be so tough to get through my morning & night routines efficiently and without forgetting something or being worried I did. This app helps me so much.

I’ve even started using it to plan out entire days or afternoons, if I have a lot of school work or a to-do list to work through. I’m taking classes and working online right now & since there’s so little natural structure in my days, it’s really tough to keep myself on track sometimes. When I’m on autopilot it’s easy to somehow get through a day without doing anything I wanted or needed to do. No matter how detailed a plan I make or how hard I try to do things in a certain order or at a certain time, I just won’t do it. But this app adds just enough extra structure / incentive to change that. Maybe it’s because once I start a “routine,” I can’t see the whole list at once, so I’m less tempted to get distracted or jump around. But now when I plan my day in the morning or the night before, I actually feel like I can stick to it (at least to some extent lol).

I’ve tried so many different apps for productivity, habit tracking, staying organized, etc. over the years, and I kind of gave up on finding one that really worked for me, but then I started looking again and found this. It’s genuinely been so helpful, as evidenced by the fact that I felt compelled to actually review an app for the first time in my life lol.

My only complaint is I wish it was a one-time payment for the premium version. Of course I wish it was free, but honestly premium has been so worth it that I’m happy to pay; I just hate having to keep track of subscriptions

title: A Straight Forward Tiny Habits / Atomic Habits app
body:
I’ve been looking for an app that fits in with the learnings and methodology from the Tiny Habits and Atomic Habits books. Both are great books which introduces a simple but powerful behavior change. Routines are great because I just tell myself, “After I wake up, I will run the morning routine.” Or “After I sit down at my office chair, I will run my Focus Routine.” 

I love the fact that the app looks nice, modern, and isn’t trying too hard. The other apps in the space that have gamification are just too complicated and it misplaced motivations. And then other apps that try and up sell you on lessons, meditation, or other content is just not something I’m looking for. 

I need a utility, not a guidance counselor.

There are a couple of drawbacks for the app. 1 is the cost. It’s a bit more expensive than I’d like and I’m not fond of subscription apps. However, given this has been the best fit for me, I was glad to pay to support the indie developer. 

The 2nd drawback is that you can’t repeat routines without resetting the history of the routine. Because I subscribe to the Tiny Habits approach of “When I do a trigger, then I will do the habit I want to build...”, I’m consistently wanting to retrigger a routine. 

It’s not a big deal given I can just restart the routine but it feels “wrong” or it would be nice if I could track my actions each time I’ve run the routine.

The great thing is that I’ve emailed the developer and the developer was receptive to my feedback. I hope there will be a future update to support repeat routines.

author: JasmineArnold

title: Great app- will be paying for premium
body:
Overall a great app. I never pay for premium apps but I’m doing the free trial and it definitely worth the 3 bucks a month. 

I recently went through a devastating breakup and I spent two weeks pretty lost, having trouble sleeping, my room was very messy, and I was always running late to work due to lack of preparation. But with this I’m able to throw myself into building heathy routines. I’ve only been using it for a few days but it is definitely so helpful. I like how visually simple the app is, it just has what I need and I don’t get overwhelmed. Already after only 4 days I am getting to sleep faster with my evening routine! 

I also have a routine set for the morning and for lunchtime at work (so I remember to stretch and meditate). 

The app has little words of encouragement that are cute too. 

I do have a few suggestions:

-make an option to set everything for military time or set it all for AM/PM. Right now it’s in regular time when you set the time for the routine, but once you start the routine it’s in 24 hour time. I’d prefer it all in AM/PM, and I’m sure some would prefer the opposite 

-add an option to move a habit to the end of the routine while the routine is running instead of just skipping it. Sometimes I want to change up the order just a little, and just once, not permanently. So if instead of skipping I could just move the habit to the end that would be great. 

-have some habits be at a certain time and other for a certain amount of time. For example, for my evening routine I first have an hour of study and then feeding my cat. But my cat needs to eat at 9pm sharp. I’d like to be able to set the feeding to always be at 9 and cut my studying short even if I haven’t completed the full hour. I know I can mark the routine as done myself but it would be nice to have the reminder instead.  

-add an option to set rewards at certain milestones of consistent habits. So that I could set it like if I complete the evening routine 4 weeks in a row I can set it to notify me and say that i get a reward, which I would have inputted myself. Previously. Make the milestones and the rewards able to be set by the users, with icons like the habits have! 

Anyways, like I said it’s a great app and I’m very happy with it! Thanks!

title: Solid App
body:
Great features and works exactly how you would expect it to! 

Feature Requests: 
- Since it tracks how much time you spend on each task, would be great to have a breakdown. In other words, sometimes some tasks might take consistently longer than you a lot for and it would be nice to know that so you can adjust your routine to be more realistic. 
- Next feature request would be to duplicate routines. I have a morning routine if I wake up late that is half as long as my normal one, would be nice to duplicate the current one. 
- Would be nice for each task within a routine to trigger a Siri shortcut or an callback link to help automate curtain habits. 

Bugs:

title: Would like to see it in a split view on iPad
body:
I really like the app.

I use the app on my iPad to help me manage time and do things faster, but I really want to use it in a split view so I can be multi-tasking and still remember to check off the ongoing task and continue to the next. 

Especially most of the apps we use very often on iPad have landscape mode, it will be a great improvement if it supports landscape mode and can be used with other apps in a split view.

Another suggestion is to add more icons for the task.

Overall, I like the app and thanks for listening to the feedback!
author: anonymous_mous

title: Great interface, but gets stuck after 5 tasks
body:
I really like the interface, but currently after the fifth task in my list, when I click “Done,” it changes the time, but doesn’t update what task I’m on. In my case, after my 5 minutes “Shower” task is done, it starts the timer for the next task, but still says “Shower” and shows the shower icon, instead of “Make coffee.” For me, that makes the app pretty much not worth using at this point.

I also would love to be able to see the rest of the list as the timers are on, so that I could tell what’s coming up next. This isn’t a big drawback, as you’re likely to know what the next step in your morning routine is, but it’s a feature that I appreciated in a very simple app called Many Timer that I used long ago until the developer discontinued it and it became incompatible with my new phone.

This app has a lot of potential, but there are some kinks to work out, and it would have to be a really great app to justify me paying a monthly subscription rather than a one-time purchase cost.
